scope: Proposition 2.4 (Closure of an exact coset) of the manuscript “The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over global function fields” (preprints/The-Margulis-Platonov-conjecture-over-global-function-fields-October-5-2026/margulis-platonov-global-function-fields.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 018 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7e90f88648f7bafc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let v0 / ∈ A, and write S(Av0 ) for the restricted product of S(kv) over v ̸= v0. Then R S(Av0 ) = {g ∈ S(Av0 ) : gA ∈ P0}. (2.5) For any γ ∈ S(k), the closure of γR is obtained by replacing P0 on the right by δA(γ)P0. In particular, all cosets γR with γ ∈ V0 have the same closure. Consequently one may approximate in an actual prescribed coset γR, meeting prescribed nonempty local open sets at finitely many isotropic places and a prescribed nonempty open subset of δA(γ)P0 at A. If x∗ ∈ U(k), the same assertion holds after left translation to the determinant slice x∗S and to the coset x∗γR. In each assertion one may also require that the resulting point lie in finitely many nonempty k-Zariski open subsets of S or x∗S, respectively.
